newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard plans PC price cuts Monday.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard plans PC price cuts Monday.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said it plans to cut prices on many of its corporate personal computers by as much as 24 percent next Monday .
H-P said late Wednesday that the price cuts would range from its small business models, commercial PCs and PC workstations.

For example, H-P said, it will offer a PC with a PentiumPro processor, fully configured, for $2,000, without a monitor. The PentiumPro system would also include 32 megabytes of memory, a 2.5 gigabyte hard drive.
H-P said its pricing moves have been in the works for several weeks and are not a reaction to Compaq Computer Corp.

H-P said another example of its new prices is a Pentium II system, at 266 megahertz, with 32 megabytes of memory and a four gigabyte hard drive, with a CD-ROM, for $2,767, a 10 percent cut. H-P said this was still a significant price cut because this PC was launched at a lower-than-average price.

Compaq is expected to announce later Thursday big price cuts in a new line of corporate PCs, as part of a new manufacturing strategy to lower its costs and compete better with direct marketer Dell Computer Corp.
"These prices are consistent with our history of pricing leadership," an H-P spokesman said.
